summary: Intermittent 429s during staggered credential rotation for orchestrated ingesters
description: Issue summary: BeaconMaps reports intermittent 429 responses for a subset of ingest workers immediately after a scheduled credential rotation. Impact: ~15% of batch uploads from their orchestrated ingester fleet fail with 429s for a ~1–3 minute window during rotations; customer sees increased retry loops and missed SLA on a handful of jobs. Frequency: Observed across 4 rotation events in the past 48 hours (2026-03-08 22:00 UTC, 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC, 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC, 2026-03-11 01:45 UTC). Customer environment: Dedicated pool (BeaconMaps-prod), long-lived orchestrated upload workers that rotate ephemeral API keys via our key-rotation endpoint. They run 12 parallel uploaders per region with staggered rotation schedule under their orchestrator.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a dedicated pool with orchestrated ingesters that rotate ephemeral credentials every 1 hour.
2) Start 8–12 parallel upload workers in us-west using multiplexed connections.
3) Trigger a rotation with overlapping refresh windows (small stagger <10s between worker groups).
4) Observe 429s in client logs during and just after rotation window.
Notes: reproduction requires parallelism + overlapping/closely-timed rotations; single-worker rotations are not reproducing the problem consistently.
logs:
[2026-03-10T02:30:01Z] upload-worker-7 POST /v1/ingest -> 429 {"error":"too_many_requests", "x-rate-limit-window":"60s"}
[2026-03-10T02:30:02Z] auth-rotator INFO swapping keys for worker-group-A (old_key=ak_...123, new_key=ak_...456)
[2026-03-10T02:30:03Z] proxy-conn-218 counted token for key ak_...123 against tenant BeaconMaps (window_start=2026-03-10T02:29:30Z)
[2026-03-10T02:30:03Z] proxy-conn-219 counted token for key ak_...456 against tenant BeaconMaps (window_start=2026-03-10T02:29:30Z)
[2026-03-10T02:30:05Z] upload-worker-3 RETRY attempt=1 after 429
[2026-03-10T02:31:10Z] upload-worker-7 SUCCESS POST /v1/ingest -> 200 (after backoff)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: overlapping rotation causes brief double-counting of tenant tokens because both old and new API key tokens are charged to the tenant window concurrently.
Checked rate-limiter logs: saw simultaneous token increments from two different API keys that both map to BeaconMaps inside the same refill window. No evidence of upstream proxy misrouting.
Observed that the customer's orchestrator triggers refresh for small groups in <10s buckets; heavy parallelism (12 workers) increases probability of >1 key being active in same 60s window.

Verified config: tenant-level window is 60s with 6k token burst configured for BeaconMaps dedicated pool. During rotation, instantaneous token counts spike above configured burst due to duplicate counting behavior.
Correlation: 4 rotation events where rotations were tightly clustered coincided with 429 spike windows on customer traces. Healthy rotations with >30s staggering did not reproduce.

Checked for related changes: no recent ingress-proxy releases in customer pool; key rotation code path change was deployed to control plane last week (PR linked below) but not directly in serving runtime.

Engineering note: candidate fix is to ensure rotation handoff marks the old key as draining (prevent new requests using both keys concurrently) OR server-side de-dup that maps rotating keys to same tenant ref and performs per-tenant dedup of near-simultaneous token accounting.
comments: 2026-03-10 04:12 - BeaconMaps (support@beaconmaps.com): We're seeing intermittent 429s right after our hourly key rotation. It affects only our mass-upload workers. Can you confirm if something changed?
2026-03-10 04:24 - Sofia Alvarez (Support): Thanks for the report — we're triaging. Can you share sample request IDs and approximate timestamps? Any recent change to your rotation stagger?
2026-03-10 05:03 - BeaconMaps: Sent sample request IDs and their worker rotation timestamps; confirmed they stagger by ~5s between groups.

2026-03-10 11:40 - Marcus Nguyen (SRE): Found double token increments in the rate-limiter logs corresponding to old and new keys mapping to the same tenant window. Adding as a linked investigation for infra.

2026-03-11 09:55 - Marcus Nguyen (SRE): Temporary mitigation deployed to customer dedicated pool: extend rotation "drain" time and apply conservative de-dupe at ingress for keys that changed in the last 30s. Monitoring in progress.

2026-03-12 02:10 - Engineering (PR): https://github.com/redwood/ingress-proxy/pull/1425 submitted (adds rotation-handoff flag + per-tenant accounting dedupe). Requesting rollout approval to BeaconMaps pool.
workaround: Short-term workaround provided to customer: 1) Increase stagger between worker-group rotations to >=30s. 2) Schedule rotations during off-peak windows. 3) As an immediate platform-side mitigation, we increased their dedicated pool burst ceiling by 50% for 2 hours around rotation windows to avoid transient 429s.
resolution_summary: Platform change merged to ingress-proxy that marks keys as 'draining' on rotation and performs per-tenant near-simultaneous accounting dedupe. Customer pool received the mitigation patch and a configuration update to ensure rotations are fenced for 30s. 429 events returned to baseline on next rotation window after patch rollout.
resolution_notes:
- Rollout steps: merge PR https://github.com/redwood/ingress-proxy/pull/1425 -> canary to internal test cluster -> deploy to BeaconMaps dedicated pool (done 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC).
- Post-deploy monitoring: 48h sliding window showed no rotation-associated 429 spikes.
- Follow-ups: update public rotation best-practices doc and add a console alert when tenant rotation density exceeds threshold.
- Owner: Marcus Nguyen (SRE) for rollout + postmortem.
